rfq.title: MA RFQ Multimodal Agents
rfq.summary: The main workflow receives text, PDFs and images and prepares a decision package before sales and engineering create an offer.
rfq.why: A technical RFQ mixes requirements, documents and internal knowledge. Handling it in one hidden prompt would conceal important steps.
rfq.purpose: Separate evidence extraction, critical review and readiness decisions while keeping final approval with a person.
rfq.how: The webhook normalises the input. Evidence Agent queries approved sources. Challenger finds contradictions. Deterministic rules calculate blockers and routing.
set: Evidence Agent with approved Markdown knowledge
rfq.state: The workflow is versioned and connected to the public demo. Credentials and company-specific rules stay outside the repository.
rfq.imageAlt: Multimodal RFQ workflow imported in the n8n editor

order.title: AuftragKlar · local order-entry pipeline
order.summary: A credential-free n8n workflow processes two fictitious orders: one valid case and one exception for human review.
order.why: Orders arrive in different formats. Extraction alone is not enough because required fields, master data, prices and special requests need separate controls.
order.purpose: Prepare the repeatable data work and hand every unusual case to a person with its rule ID and source.
order.how: Manual Trigger provides two synthetic orders. Code nodes normalise fields and check required data plus fictitious customer and article masters. An IF node separates the ERP-ready draft from the exception record.
set: One local n8n workflow without credentials
Two synthetic orders and fictitious master data
JSON/CSV draft, exception object and audit log
order.state: The workflow is versioned in the private research workspace and runs locally. The public case study does not link that repository. There is no OCR, external transmission or ERP write access.
order.imageAlt: Architecture diagram of the local AuftragKlar workflow with valid and human-review branches

rag.title: Second Brain · Capture, ask and protect
rag.summary: A group of workflows classifies notes, detects duplicates, stores them in Supabase and answers questions about them. The security lab started after testing how a note could also try to give orders to the RAG system.
rag.why: Capturing knowledge, retrieving notes and testing their security are different responsibilities. Separating them makes the stored data, model context and supporting sources visible.
rag.purpose: Keep a searchable second brain while preventing hidden instructions inside a note from changing assistant behaviour.
rag.how: Capture tags and prepares the note, Ask retrieves bounded context, and the lab runs prompt-injection attacks. A script exports the notes from the repository for review in Obsidian.
set: Capture: classification, tags, duplicate detection and ingestion
Ask: search, bounded context, answer and citations
Security Lab and note export for Obsidian
rag.state: The public demo uses synthetic notes to show attacks and defences. Personal Supabase and model-provider credentials are configured outside the repository.
rag.imageAlt: Second Brain Ask workflow imported in the n8n editor

fridge.title: Telegram Audio Intake v2
fridge.summary: The workflow turns a Telegram voice note into a clear fridge operation: add, update or remove an item.
fridge.why: A phrase such as ‘we have half a carton of milk left’ does not map directly to a database row. The system first needs to understand the item, quantity and intent.
fridge.purpose: Maintain the inventory by speaking while keeping an application where the saved result can be checked or corrected.
fridge.how: Telegram receives the audio, the flow transcribes it, AI creates a structured event, and deterministic rules add, update or remove the Supabase record. The application shows the result.
set: 01 Audio Intake v2: receipt, voice, validation and inventory
90 Error Handler: classification and safe notification
InventoryEvent contract shared with the application
fridge.state: The public demo uses a synthetic fridge. The voice path connects Telegram, transcription and Supabase when the environment credentials are added.
fridge.imageAlt: FridgeFlow audio workflow imported in the n8n editor

agent.title: Agent Chaos Lab · 03 Orchestrator
agent.summary: The experiment app starts a webhook and provides basic CRUD controls for Supabase. n8n coordinates several agents while Agent Observatory shows each round at runtime.
agent.why: One giant workflow would hide the kill switch, GitHub permissions and the decision to continue another round.
agent.purpose: Experiment with agents that propose changes, prepare GitHub modifications and leave an inspectable trace that can be stopped.
agent.how: The app calls the webhook. Orchestrator runs Explorer, Builder, GitHub Commit and Observer, checks Control Gate before continuing, and stores messages and events in Supabase.
set: Public Start, Control Gate and Orchestrator
Explorer, Builder, GitHub Commit and Observer
agent.state: The app, Observatory and nine workflow JSON files are publicly inspectable. The guided trace uses synthetic data; Supabase, n8n and GitHub credentials stay private.
agent.imageAlt: Agent Chaos Lab Orchestrator workflow imported in the n8n editor

music.title: Music School Enquiry
music.summary: A small workflow receives a structured enquiry, validates the fields and prepares a short notification for the person managing the school.
music.why: A family needs to ask about a course and schedule without understanding internal planning or completing a long form.
music.purpose: Turn the enquiry into a clear Telegram message while leaving the reply and final confirmation with a person.
music.how: The webhook receives course, level, day and contact. A deterministic step validates the payload and the Telegram node notifies the configured administrator.
set: The final reply is always human
music.state: The public demo shows the enquiry path with example data. Telegram activates when the bot is configured; Twilio is a possible call-handling extension, not part of the current demo.

approachPage.title: The difference is in how the system is checked.
approachPage.lead: I build a surface that makes the flow understandable, separate decisions from effects and document what has not been validated yet.

evidence.title: Start with proof you can open
evidence.copy: The interface shows the path with synthetic data and lets people inspect the result without preparing private infrastructure.
evidence.detail: The demo is not the integration. It helps agree on behaviour, language and decisions before connecting real systems.
evidence.result: Something concrete to discuss from day one.

human.title: Human review is part of the design
human.copy: When a decision can affect a customer, inventory or repository, the workflow prepares evidence and keeps final control with a person.
human.detail: Models can extract or propose. Rules control routing, and sensitive effects need an explicit boundary.

boundaries.title: Scope stays next to the project
boundaries.copy: Each case explains the complete product and adds one short note about the data and services used by its public demo.
boundaries.detail: This keeps the flow readable without filling the page with repeated technical labels or confusing a preview with a connected integration.
boundaries.result: The project comes first and its boundaries remain clear.

delivery.title: Build, tests and documentation are the delivery
delivery.copy: Repositories include instructions, architecture, screenshots and reproducible checks before GitHub Pages publication.
delivery.detail: Credentials, customer documents and personal data stay out. Changes are checked on desktop and mobile and deployed from the repository.
delivery.result: A base another person can inspect and continue.

approachPage.closingTitle: A demo you can open and an architecture you can discuss.

rfq.name: Menz RFQ Copilot
rfq.summary: A fit check for complex technical requests before an offer is prepared.
rfq.problem: Sales and engineering receive requirements spread across forms, email and documents. Contradictions can surface late.
rfq.solution: Structures the request, separates evidence from questions, flags contradictions and prepares precise customer questions.
rfq.how: Text, PDFs and images pass through evidence extraction, critical review and readiness rules. A person keeps the final decision before offer work begins.
rfq.try: Load the example RFQ and inspect the decision, blockers, sources and reply draft.
rfq.scope: The demo uses a synthetic RFQ. Each company configures its own rules, internal knowledge and credentials in its environment.
rfq.imageAlt: Menz RFQ Copilot analysing a synthetic technical request

order.name: AuftragKlar
order.summary: Independent product research into controlled order entry: fictitious orders are checked and prepared as ERP-ready drafts.
order.problem: Orders arrive as email, CSV or documents. Required fields, customers, articles, prices and special requests need clarification before a system hand-off.
order.solution: A local prototype structures the order, applies deterministic rules and separates valid cases from exceptions that need a person.
order.how: CSV, TXT and EML are read locally; PDF/XLSX remain explicit adapter payloads. Fictitious master data checks customer, article and price. Only an approved case gets a JSON/CSV draft; no ERP is written.
order.try: Open the public case study and inspect the market basis, inputs, rules, exception handling, implementation status and limits.
flow: Match customer, article and price against fictitious masters
Log an ERP-ready draft or a human exception
order.scope: Market-backed prototype and local demo, not a customer or production system. The analysis covers 1,576 job postings; 448 describe the dominant process from order receipt to ERP preparation or entry. No ERP connection and no proven savings.
order.imageAlt: Local AuftragKlar demo with a fictitious order, validation rules and exception review

rag.name: Second Brain
rag.summary: An application that stores notes, organises them with AI and answers questions about them, with a lab that shows how the RAG flow is protected.
rag.problem: Notes grow, duplicate and become hard to retrieve. A note can also contain instructions that try to redirect the assistant's answer.
rag.solution: Classifies, tags, detects duplicates and stores notes in Supabase. It then answers questions and tests the retrieval path against prompt injection.
rag.how: When a note is saved, AI proposes a category and tags. Ask retrieves sourced fragments. The lab reproduces malicious notes, documents failures and compares the original flow with a hardened one. A script exports notes for Obsidian.
rag.try: Run three attacks with synthetic notes, edit the content and compare what the exposed flow accepts with what the hardened flow blocks.
flow: Store content and metadata in Supabase
Ask questions with retrieval and citations
Export to Obsidian and run security tests
rag.scope: The public demo focuses on the security lab and uses synthetic notes. Personal Supabase and model credentials are not published.
rag.imageAlt: RAG security lab comparing exposed and hardened retrieval workflows

fridge.name: FridgeFlow
fridge.summary: A fridge inventory that can also be maintained by sending voice notes through Telegram.
fridge.problem: Updating a household list manually is tedious, and spoken language does not map directly to database fields.
fridge.solution: AI understands the audio, maps it to an inventory structure and proposes adding, updating or removing the right item.
fridge.how: Telegram receives the audio. n8n transcribes it and creates a validated InventoryEvent. Deterministic rules apply the operation in Supabase, and the UI lets a person inspect and manage the result.
fridge.try: Explore the example fridge, inspect priorities and activity, and see how a voice input is represented as structured data.
flow: Send a voice note through Telegram
Add, update or remove in Supabase
Review the result in the application
fridge.scope: The public demo uses a synthetic household. The connected path needs environment credentials for Telegram, transcription and Supabase.
fridge.imageAlt: FridgeFlow showing food priorities with synthetic data

agent.name: Agent Chaos Lab
agent.summary: An app starts a multi-agent experiment; n8n coordinates the rounds and Agent Observatory shows what happens.
agent.problem: When several agents propose and apply changes, it is hard to know who decided what, what reached GitHub and how to stop the next round.
agent.solution: Separates the entry app, Supabase CRUD service, n8n orchestration, GitHub writes and runtime monitoring in Agent Observatory.
agent.how: The button calls the webhook and the basic controls use the CRUD service. Explorer, Builder and Observer exchange messages; the flow prepares GitHub changes for review and records events in Supabase. Observatory displays conversations, commits, events and the kill switch.
agent.try: Open the experiment app to see the webhook and CRUD controls. Then open Observatory and inspect one run, agent messages and external controls.
flow: Start from the app or change data through CRUD
Record and monitor the run in Observatory
agent.scope: The app, Observatory and workflows are public. The guided trace uses synthetic data and n8n, Supabase and GitHub credentials stay outside the repository.
agent.imageAlt: Agent Observatory showing a synthetic multi-agent trace

music.name: Music School Automation
music.summary: An application for course and timetable enquiries that hands each request to the right person through Telegram.
music.problem: A family wants to know which class and time fit without understanding internal planning or waiting to reach someone by phone.
music.solution: Guides course, level, day and contact, validates the enquiry and sends the administrator a short summary for reply.
music.how: The application creates a clear payload. n8n validates the fields and Telegram notifies the school. A person still replies and confirms the place.
music.try: Choose an example course, complete the enquiry and inspect exactly what information the school receives.
flow: Reply and confirm with a person
music.scope: The public demo shows the enquiry and preview with example data. Real delivery activates when the Telegram bot is configured.
music.extension: Twilio could receive or route calls and turn them into the same structured enquiry. This integration is not part of the current demo.
music.imageAlt: Music School application with synthetic courses and enquiry form
